full_judgment:
2. The present respondent No. 2, Abdul Khaleque Chowdhury as petitioner filed the aforesaid writ petition challenging the legality of Memo No. Je: Pro:/Cox/SA/7-19/2009/ 2175 dated 23-11-2009 stating, inter alia, that 7.27 acres of land of Khatian No. 1, Plot No. 2262 originally belonged to Abdul Bari Peshker and the said Abdul Bari Peshker while owning and possessing the same died leaving behind four sons namely, Fazlul Karim, Bazlur Rahim, Abu Bakar Siddique and Abu Teher. The MRR Khatian was accordingly prepared in their names. Abu Bakar Siddique, subsequently sold out 88 decimals of land out of the said 7.27 acres of land (hereinafter referred to as the case land) by an unregistered sale deed dated 7-7-1969 and delivered possession thereof to the writ petitioner. The writ petitioner while enjoying the case land on paying rent to the Government, it had gone under river Bankkhali and lost by diluvion during the year 1971- 1972. Thereafter, the case land was recorded in the name of the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar under Khatian No. 1 as Plot No. 2262. Subsequently, 54.04 acres of land including the case land re-appeared in situ by alluvion between the years 1995 to 2000 and became cultivable. In 2000, Abdul Khaleque Chowdhury made an application for leasing out the said 54.04 acres of land including the case land in his favour. Upon inquiry, the Tashilder of Union Land Office, Cox's Bazar submitted a report on 12-9-2000 to the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Sadar, Cox's Bazar mentioning that the land had become cultivable. Whereupon, the Assistant Commissioner recommended for placing the said application to the "Shrimp Mahal Committee" for consideration. Thereupon, the writ petitioner made a representation on 5-10-2000 to the concerned authority for allotment of the case land in his favour. But it was kept in abeyance. So, the writ petitioner filed another application for allotment of case land under section 86 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (shortly, the SA&T Act) as amended by Act No. 15 of 1994 (hereinafter referred to as the Amending Act). The concerned authority i.e. the Deputy Commissioner and District Collector, Cox's Bazar rejected the said application by Memo dated 23-11-2009., Abdul Khaleque Chowdhury thereafter filed Writ Petition No. 98 of 2010 and obtained a rule. 

 3. Upon hearing, the High Court Division made the rule absolute and thereby declared that the Memo dated 23-11-2009 of the Revenue Deputy Collector, Cox's Bazar to have been issued without lawful authority and be of no legal effect. The High Court Division also directed the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar to release the case property in favour of the writ petitioner under section 86 (5) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. 

 "The case of the writ petitioner is that his predecessor owned 7.27 acres of land which was lost by diluvion. His claim to allotment therefore, extends to the maximum quantum of land owned by him or his predecessor before the loss by diluvion. But the quantum of Land to be allotted is subject to the restriction in section 86(5), i.e. together with the land already held by him the total quantum of land shall not exceed sixty standard bighas. Accordingly, the respondent is hereby directed to allot as much of the case land to the writ petitioner as is permitted by law under section 86 (5) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950." 

 9. Mr Md Nurul Amin, the learned senior Advocate for the appellants after taking us through the leave granting order submits that respondent No. 2, Abdul Khaleque Chowdhury was never a tenant of the land in question. Besides, this Division although did not recognize him as tenant directed respondent No. 1, the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar to allot the case land to the respondent No.2 (writ petitioner) under section 86(5) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 which is barred by law and, as such, the judgment and order dated 10-10-2013 passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2120 of 2011 is liable to be reviewed. 

 14. Mr Probir Neogi, the learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr Mohammad Hossain, the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 2 submits that on 13-7-1994 the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 was amended substituting section 86 with a new section 86. Section 86(2) provides that the right, title and interest of the original tenant or his successor-in-interest shall subsist in the land during period of loss by diluvion if such lands re-appear in situ within 30 years of their loss. Under section 86(3) the collector is to take immediate possession of the land and under section 86(5) the collector would allot the land to the tenant whose land was diluviated. 

 15. He further submits that the order impugned by this respondent in the writ petition was passed in gross violation of the provision of section 86(2) and (5) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and hence the same suffers from malice in law and therefore without jurisdiction and void and the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute and this Hon'ble Court has rightly passed the order dated 10-10-2013 in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2120 of 2011. Section 86(2) and (5) of the Act of 1950 are applicable to lands what have alluviated after 13-7-1994 and within 30 years of diluvion and hence the impugned order was rightly set-aside by the High Court Division. Under section 86(5) of the Act of 1950 this respondent is entitle to be allotted the case land therefore the appeal is liable to be dismissed. 

 "In view of the use of the words, 'the right, title and interest of the tenant or his successor-in-interest shall subsist' during the period of loss if the land re-appear in situ within thirty years of loss is so clear and unambiguous that the legislature intended this provision to have prospective operation. The use of the word 'shall' is taken to indicate that the statute is to be construed as prospective only. The words 'within thirty years of loss' means if the diluvion takes place after 13th July, 1994, the tenant or his successor's right to re-possession shall subsist if the diluviated land re-appear within thirty years of loss and not otherwise. The amendment is prospective in operation and the High Court Division is not correct in giving retrospective operation of the substituted provision of sub-section (2) of section 86 of the Act of 1950." 

 24. Therefore, it is abundantly clear that if the respondent No. 2 (writ petitioner) was the bonafide owner or the successors-in-interest of the original tenant of the case land before the loss by diluvion, would be entitled to get allotment when his claim is permitted by law under section 86(5) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950.
